title: Google DeepMind releases searchable map of every possible DNA letter change
summary: A 1-petabyte precomputed Atlas puts billions of regulatory predictions behind a free browser to filter the 98% non-coding genome, but its ranking score is uncalibrated for clinical use and every hit still needs lab proof.

claims.text: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome Atlas on 8 September 2026 containing precomputed predictions for all ~9 billion possible single-nucleotide variants in the human genome (every position × 3 alternative bases).

claims.text: ACMG/AMP 2015 guidelines (Richards et al., Genet Med 17:405-423) limit computational (in silico) predictor evidence to supporting-level only (PP3 for pathogenic, BP4 for benign), explicitly warning 'Not overestimating computational evidence is important, particularly given that different algorithms may rely on the same (or similar) data to support predictions and most algorithms have not been validated against well-established pathogenic variants' and that 'algorithms can have vastly different predictive capabilities for different genes.' If predictions disagree, evidence cannot be counted as supporting. This constrains AVI to supporting at most without independent ClinGen calibration.

sources.title: Standards and guidelines for the interpretation of sequence variants: a joint consensus recommendation of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association for Molecular Pathology

claims.text: ClinGen Sequence Variant Interpretation Working Group calibration (Pejaver et al. 2022 Am J Hum Genet 109:2163-2177, expanded Bergquist et al. 2025 Genet Med 27:101402) found only 4 of 13 evaluated tools could reach PP3 strong, 9 topped out at moderate/supporting, and GERP++ failed to meet even PP3 supporting; CADD's developer-recommended threshold of 20.0 falls within BP4 moderate range, meaning it was being misapplied as pathogenic evidence. REVEL is the only tool covering PP3 strong (≥0.932) to BP4 very strong (≤0.003). AVI (18-feature model trained on allele-frequency threshold as rarity proxy) is not among ClinGen-calibrated tools and has no published PP3/BP4 thresholds; clinical labs therefore cannot apply it above supporting without formal calibration.

sources.title: How AI Prediction Tools Are Changing Rare Disease Diagnosis — ACMG PP3 Evidence Strength, REVEL, and 3Cnet (summarizing Pejaver et al. 2022 and Bergquist et al. 2025)

claims.text: Variant-effect predictor benchmarks are inflated by Type 1 circularity (same variant in train and test) and Type 2 circularity (same gene in train and test even with distinct variants), especially where genes have all-benign or all-pathogenic labels; ensemble methods (REVEL, MetaLR) and supervised models are prone to this bias. In a 46-method comparison, only 19 methods met criteria for unbiased clinical evaluation (not trained on ClinVar/HGMD, not using features from such methods, not using allele frequency), because 'the vast majority... have been trained on clinical databases like ClinVar, leading to circularity issues.' AVI's training on allele-frequency threshold and inclusion of conservation/LoF features risks similar allele-frequency leakage, and the 22/24 and 25/26 (vs preprint 24/26) SOTA claims depend on comparator and task selection.

claims.text: Independent genomic-model developer Carl de Boer (University of British Columbia, author of framework for comparing models like AlphaGenome) called AlphaGenome the 'field's leading model' but 'very slow and computationally intensive,' and warned the Atlas single-number AVI score 'has a clear use, but it also is probably going to be easily misinterpreted. We're talking about a very complex system, and there's a lot of moving parts.' He and IEEE Spectrum note the 1 Mb receptive field misses enhancers acting over longer distances, and many diseases involve multiple variants, limiting single-variant scores.

sources.title: AlphaGenome Atlas Maps 9 Billion Possible DNA Variants

claims.text: Precomputed 1 PB Atlas trades on-demand freshness for convenience: locked to hg38 reference, no ancestry breakdown or false-positive rate for AVI disclosed in DeepMind post, no bulk-download/egress pricing, and commercial access requires separate Google Cloud license (non-commercial free) — a two-tier structure unlike AlphaFold DB's fully open release. This creates equity and staleness risks: reference-genome bias, inability to update for new cell types or hg38 successors without recomputation, and pharma/academic access asymmetry.

claims.text: Hybrid predictors that integrate protein structure, multiple sequence alignments, or population genetics data gain accuracy but add complexity, limited applicability where data are unavailable, and circularity risk; sequence-only PLM versions of TranceptEVE and SaProt 'decrease substantially' without MSA/3D structure, and 'the use of population genetics data can lead to data circularity concerns in clinical genetics applications.' This frames AVI's design choice (10 AlphaGenome + AlphaMissense + conservation + LoF + indel features trained on rarity) as inheriting both the power and the circularity/interpretability tradeoffs of hybrid models.
